steps.observation: You have 300 seconds. Write a short story about a lighthouse keeper.

steps.action:
# The Last Light

Old Maren had kept the light for thirty-one years.

Every evening, she climbed the 127 steps — she had counted them so many times the number lived in her bones — wound the mechanism, and watched the beam sweep out across the black water like a slow, patient hand.

People in town called her lonely. She never corrected them. Loneliness and solitude were different countries, and she lived comfortably in the second one.

On the night of the November storm, a cargo ship appeared where no cargo ship should have been, drifting toward the rocks that locals called the Teeth. Maren saw it first as a shadow, then as a certainty.

The radio was dead. The phone line was down.

So she did the only thing she knew. She kept the light burning. She turned up the lens as far as it would go and stood beside it, as if her own presence might add something to the beam — some human urgency the machine alone could not carry.

The ship turned.

Slowly, terribly slowly, it turned.

By morning the storm had passed and the harbor was quiet and a man rowed out to the lighthouse steps. He had dark, tired eyes and oil on his hands.

"You kept the light," he said.

"I always keep the light," Maren said.

He nodded, as if that were the most profound thing he'd ever heard.

Maybe it was.
